title: Refactor CI task scheduler, add dep-eviction protector, and quiet-release window automation
author: Maya Patel
commits: Rewrite CI scheduler to weight-based queueing (initial impl)
Add dep-eviction-protector service and slim API for coordinator
Introduce quiet-release-window hook and gating in release-orchestrator
Move heavy integration tests to staggered pool and add early lint fast-fail
Add docs and telemetry for scheduler decisions and eviction events
description:
Context: Our presubmit/test matrix has continued to grow and causes long tail latency for merges and flakey capacity interference with Dedicated pools. This PR refactors the CI task scheduler to use a lightweight, weight-based queue and introduces a dep-eviction-protector service to reduce release thrash when dependency updates or cache refreshes cause transient worker eviction. It also adds a quiet-release-window mechanism in the release orchestrator to ensure release automation does not overlap with scheduled maintenance or bulk dep-rolls.

What this changes (high level):
- Replace matrix-first scheduler with a weight-based scheduler that considers job type (lint/unit/integration), estimated runtime, and cache-affinity. This enables fast-fail lint early and defers heavy integration jobs into staggered pools.
- New dep-eviction-protector service (small Go binary under tools/ci/eviction-protector) that tracks in-flight dep-refreshes and pins a small portion of runners to avoid simultaneous eviction during rolling updates. Interaction with autoscaler is via a thin HTTP health API.
- Quiet-release-window: release-orchestrator now checks calendar windows and a release-lock store before starting automation; manual override supported for urgent fixes.
- Cache improvements: prewarm step added for high-fanout jobs to reduce cold-start IO.
- Observability: added metrics for scheduler decisions, eviction-protector events, and quiet-window triggers; dashboard links in doc.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement weight-based scheduler (basic policy + config knobs)
- [x] Implement eviction-protector service and health API
- [x] Integrate quiet-release-window checks into release-orchestrator
- [x] Migrate presubmit job groups to new scheduler policies
- [x] Add unit tests for scheduler and eviction-protector logic
- [x] Add integration smoke test for quiet-window enforcement
- [x] Add docs and runbook for SRE on how to handle protector alerts

Motivation: We observed multiple incidents where Dependabot-style batch updates coincided with cache churn in Dedicated pools, causing spiky evictions and a cascade of rebuild jobs that pushed CI latency above our SLO. The protector reduces simultaneous evictions; the scheduler reduces tail latency by prioritizing fast feedback. Quiet-release-window prevents automated releases from starting during noisy maintenance windows.

Compatibility & migration notes: The new scheduler is opt-in via a per-repo config flag (ci/scheduler.yaml). Default policy keeps existing behavior until teams flip the flag. Eviction-protector runs as a small deployment in infra namespace for Dedicated and as a sidecar-lite when on-hosted CI. Release-orchestrator has a backward-compatible check - if the calendar store is unreachable, it falls back to previous behavior but emits an alert.

Docs and runbook: See docs/ci/scheduler.md and docs/ci/eviction-protector-runbook.md in this PR.

Related: Linear ENG-2982 (reduce CI tail latency), ENG-3010 (reduce release flakiness). Support ticket SUP-4121 tracks a customer-facing incident that motivated the quick protector patch.

Merge notes: Squash-merged to main after CI flakiness was addressed (see CI history).
review_conversation: Aaron Chen: Nice approach — can you explain how the weight model maps to existing job labels? Suggest we add a 'non-blocking' label to force low-cost scheduling for docs jobs.
Maya Patel: Reply: Added mapping table to ci/presubmit/policies.md and implemented support for 'non-blocking' tag. Docs job mapping included.
Priya Reddy: The protector health API needs authentication gating before autoscaler integration. Right now it's unauthenticated. Please add a token check or RBAC.
Maya Patel: Reply: Switched to a mTLS-enabled health endpoint and added a short-lived token flow for autoscaler in infra/k8s manifests. Details in runbook.
Luca Moretti: Observability looks good; can you emit an event when a job is deferred due to quiet-window to help triage?
Maya Patel: Reply: Added an event emission and a dedicated metric `ci_release_deferred_total` sent to the controller; dashboard updated.
Aaron Chen: CI initially failed on the smoke integration flake — re-ran and it passed. Approving now.
Priya Reddy: Approved after RBAC change and small test fix.
release_notes: Introduce weight-based CI scheduler to reduce tail latency; add dep-eviction-protector to minimize worker churn during batch dependency updates; enforce quiet-release-window for release automation. See docs/ci/* for configuration and runbook.
